checks_run.note: The run exited successfully. The output was too large to display and its file was outside the working directory, so I did not see per-test counts. `cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test retry` separately showed 5 passed.

open_issues: Because the logic lives in `earlier_attempt()`, a hand-typed 'try again on <job>' also gets the introspection section. The two share one code path, and the reader brief is rebuilt from the stored request text on a re-read. The CHANGELOG says so.

Nothing records whether a prevention was acted on, because the 'acted-on' status is a later build. 'Already tried' therefore means 'proposed in an earlier case of the same class', and the brief says the class recurred.
The `--json` output has no field saying whether the retry was seeded from the introspection. The fallback notice goes to stderr only.
I did not touch run.rs, status.rs, introspect.rs or display.rs, which the brief listed as possible deliverables. The existing code paths already cover them.
mistakes: My first draft of the retry test queued only one introspection reply for two jobs, so the second rejection's introspection failed. I restructured it so a reply is queued after the correction and before the run.
The first `cargo check` failed on imports I had guessed from `athena_data` instead of `athena_data::records`.
learnings: Records::introspections is oldest-first; IntrospectionRecord and its enums are exported from athena_data::records, and JobState from athena_core::store.
The fake script in tests/common runs the introspection step through the same driver, so tests recognise it by its system prompt starting 'You write one introspection'.
A correction is introspected immediately. With no scripted reply it records a failed introspection and does not break the command.
Bash is limited to cargo, git and ls, so a long `cargo test` output cannot be searched afterwards.
desires: A way to read large test output files from tool results.
A shell-free way to run a single test and see only its summary.
